claims.text: Isothermal aging of HfNbTaTiZr at 650 °C progressively increases short-range chemical order as aging duration increases from 5 to 30 hours.
The rapid-quenched, solution-treated baseline has minimal preexisting short-range order.
Short-range chemical order creates localized lattice distortions in HfNbTaTiZr.
Short-range chemical order modifies local interatomic bonding environments.
Aging-induced short-range order changes lattice parameters.
Changes in lattice parameters and bonding environments alter local stress fields.
The altered local stress fields affect dislocation glide.
Changes in dislocation glide influence high-temperature creep behavior.
Short-range order modifies elastic moduli by changing lattice stiffness and interatomic distances.
Short-range order modifies thermal expansion through changes in lattice stiffness and interatomic distances.
Samples with greater short-range order will have higher yield stress than the quenched baseline.
Samples with greater short-range order will have lower creep rates at 1250 °C than the quenched baseline.
Samples with greater short-range order will exhibit shifted elastic-modulus profiles from 293 to 1100 K relative to the quenched baseline.
Samples with greater short-range order will exhibit shifted thermal-expansion profiles relative to the quenched baseline.
Synchrotron X-ray or neutron scattering can quantitatively distinguish the degrees of short-range order produced by the aging treatments.
Concurrent microstructural phenomena may influence the quantitative relationship between short-range order and the measured properties.
Detecting and correlating short-range order with mechanical and thermoelastic responses may be limited by measurement sensitivity.
